Suppression is closely related to repression yet it is distinctive in its own way. Suppression is a deliberate, conscious act to cover up a wish or desire. Unlike repression, suppression occurs with some awareness by the person. A person using suppression is somewhat aware that he/she is using this defense mechanism

Let's look at some examples

Repression: A child has the urge to his his father. However, this is unpleasant to the child so he wishes that impulse out of existence. He says and believes that he never had such an impulse

Suppression: A child has the urge to hit his father but acts as if he had no such feeling. The child is aware of the feeling but takes measures to keep it hidden.
